sections.h2: Where is the Marquette County Register of Deeds and what are its hours?
sections.html:
The Marquette County Register of Deeds sits at 234 W. Baraga Avenue in Marquette, Michigan 49855, and the office phone is (906) 225-8415. The county lists office hours as Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Electronic submissions can arrive at any hour but are worked during the 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. window.

The county site describes the office as the official recording point for every land record in the county, going back to the 1800s. Michigan follows a race-notice rule, so the order in which documents reach the counter decides priority. A deed that is recorded first protects the buyer against later claims, which is why a closing agent usually records the same day funds move.

Three county offices that touch a house sale share the same courthouse address:

  • Register of Deeds, for deeds, mortgages, discharges and copies
  • County Treasurer, for the tax certificate and delinquent real property taxes, at (906) 225-8425
  • Equalization and Tax Roll, for ownership records, parcel maps and assessment questions, at (906) 225-8405

sections.h2: What does the Marquette County housing picture look like for a seller?
sections.html:
Marquette County covers 1,808 square miles of land, which makes it the largest Michigan county by land area, and it is the most populous county in the Upper Peninsula. Lake Superior forms its northern edge. The Census Bureau estimated 68,064 residents on July 1, 2025, up 2.3 percent from the April 2020 estimates base.

QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024 put the median value of an owner-occupied home at $216,500 and the owner-occupied rate at 69.6 percent. Median gross rent was $949, and the median household income was $65,429. Marquette, Ishpeming and Negaunee are the three cities, and Northern Michigan University, founded in 1899, anchors the county seat.

The Marquette Iron Range, the Cliffs Shaft Mine and the Jackson Mine are among the county's ten state historical markers. Parcels around the range towns can have long chains of title, so ask the title company how far back it will search before closing.

sections.h2: How much does it cost to record a deed in Marquette County?
sections.html:
Recording a deed in Marquette County costs $30.00 per document, no matter how many pages it runs. The county states that the figure already includes the Michigan remonumentation fee and the automation fee, so no extra surcharge is added at the counter.

Marquette County Register of Deeds charges published on the county fee schedule
ServiceCharge
Record a deed, mortgage or lis pendens$30.00
Each added instrument assigned or discharged in one document$3.00
Treasurer tax certification, when the document needs one$5.00
Certify a recorded document$5.00
Copy of a recorded document, per page$1.00
Plat copy, per page$2.00
Grantor/grantee search, per year searched$0.50 (minimum $5.00)

Transfer tax and the treasurer's certification are charged on top of the recording fee when the document calls for them. The office accepts cash, check or credit card, and card payments carry a processing fee.

sections.h2: Who pays Michigan transfer tax when a Marquette County house sells?
sections.html:
The seller pays. Marquette County's transfer tax page places the tax on the grantor and requires the deed to state the full consideration, so the sale price must appear on the face of the document or in a valuation affidavit.

The state portion is $3.75 for each $500 of value or fraction of $500 (MCL 207.525). On a $200,000 sale that is 400 units, or $1,500 in state tax, and the county portion is added to it. Ask the Register of Deeds for the county figure at your price before you set a net-proceeds number.

Some conveyances are exempt under MCL 207.526, and the exemption has to be written on the face of the deed. The ones that come up most often in family and distressed sales are:

  • A deed given for consideration under $100
  • A conveyance from a parent or grandparent to a child or grandchild
  • A transfer made in foreclosure or by deed in lieu of foreclosure
  • A land contract, until legal title passes
  • A quitclaim used only to correct a flaw in title

No fee applies to filing the valuation affidavit itself. The deed simply needs a line saying that the affidavit is on file.

sections.h2: What must a deed look like before Marquette County will record it?
sections.html:
The deed has to meet MCL 565.201 and the county's own checks. The office does not draft documents or give legal advice, and it accepts only instruments with original signatures, so a fax or a plain photocopy will be turned away.

The statute asks for the following on every instrument signed after April 1, 1997:

  • Each signer's name printed or typed beneath the signature, in black or dark blue ink
  • A match between those names and the notary acknowledgment
  • The notary's printed name near the signature
  • The street or post office address of every grantee
  • The name and business address of the person who drafted the deed
  • A single first-line statement of the recordable event, such as "Warranty Deed"
  • A 2 1/2 inch blank margin at the top of page one and 1/2 inch elsewhere, 10-point type, white paper of at least 20-pound weight
  • The first five digits of any Social Security number removed

A court order recorded against a Marquette County parcel must be a certified copy. The county FAQ says a "true copy" of a court document will not be accepted.

sections.h2: Does a Marquette County deed need a tax certificate from the treasurer?
sections.html:
A warranty deed, a deed with a covenant of warranty, a land contract or an assignment of one does need it. Under MCL 211.135 the register of deeds must see proof that taxes on the parcel are paid for the five years before the date of the instrument. A quitclaim deed with no warranty is excused from that rule.

The Marquette County Treasurer works from the Courthouse Annex at 234 W. Baraga Avenue and is open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The county treasurer collects delinquent real property taxes: townships and cities send over what is unpaid every March 1, and the treasurer accepts debit and credit card payments on those delinquent bills. A seller who is behind should clear the delinquency before the certificate is requested, or have the title company pay it from proceeds at closing.

The register of deeds notifies the local assessor about recorded transfers at least once a month. The buyer must also file a transfer notice with the assessing office within 45 days (MCL 211.27a), and the taxable value generally resets to the state equalized value the year after the sale.

sections.h2: How do I search Marquette County land records or record a deed electronically?
sections.html:
The county's online database holds deed images and index entries from January 1, 1980, and mortgage and miscellaneous documents from January 1, 1983. Anything older is reached in person at the office. Copies of pre-1983 records carry a $7.50 tract fee on top of the $1.00 per page copy charge, according to the county FAQ.

The office accepts electronic recording through four vendors named on its eRecording page: CSC, ePN, Indecomm Global Services and Simplifile. Not every document type can go this way, so title companies check with the vendor first. A rejected document comes back by the same route.

The register of deeds also warns about outside companies that sell certified deed copies for $50 or more. Copies of any land record cost as little as $1 per page from the county itself, and the office runs a free Property Fraud Alert sign-up for owners.

faqs.q: How much is the Marquette County recording fee?
faqs.a: The county charges $30.00 per document regardless of page count. That figure includes the state remonumentation and register of deeds automation fees. A $3.00 charge applies for each additional instrument assigned or discharged in the same document.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax in Marquette County?
faqs.a: The seller, or grantor, is liable. The state rate is $3.75 per $500 of value, and the county adds its own amount. Exempt transfers, such as a deed from a parent to a child, must state the exemption on the face of the deed.

faqs.q: Can I record a copy of my deed in Marquette County?
faqs.a: No. The register of deeds records only documents carrying original signatures, and court documents must be certified by the court. Ask the office before you mail anything so it can confirm the paperwork is complete.

faqs.q: Do I need a tax certificate to sell my Marquette County house?
faqs.a: Yes for a warranty deed or land contract. MCL 211.135 requires proof that the property taxes for the previous five years are paid. The treasurer's certification costs $5.00 according to the register of deeds fee schedule.

faqs.q: How far back do Marquette County online records go?
faqs.a: Deed images and the index start January 1, 1980, and mortgages and miscellaneous documents start January 1, 1983. Older records are available in person at the Baraga Avenue office.
